title: The Downside of Creating Good Habits
coreMove: Detect when a habit has stopped teaching you and deliberately disrupt its autopilot before competence calcifies into complacency.

exampleSpecs.domain: a pediatric ICU nurse who has done the same handoff checklist 4,000 times and almost misses a med-pump alarm because the ritual itself feels like attention
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinician whose expertise is now also their biggest blind spot
exampleSpecs.stakes: a child whose deteriorating vitals are hidden behind a checklist that has become background noise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she catches the moment her habit replaced her noticing, and reintroduces a deliberate pause before signing off

exampleSpecs.domain: a jazz pianist preparing for a club residency who realizes his nightly practice routine has frozen into the same three voicings he was good at two years ago
exampleSpecs.audience: a working musician whose discipline is no longer producing growth
exampleSpecs.stakes: a six-month residency that will sound like the last six months unless he breaks his own pattern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he distinguishes the comfort of repetition from the work of refinement, and rewrites one practice block to force a measurable error rate

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional bakery manager whose 5am opening routine is so smooth she stopped tasting the bread
exampleSpecs.audience: an operator whose systems run her shop better than her judgment does
exampleSpecs.stakes: a slow drift in product quality that customers are starting to feel before she does
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she chooses a small piece of friction (a daily blind taste against yesterday's loaf) to put noticing back inside the routine

exampleSpecs.domain: a couples therapist and his wife of nineteen years who realize their Sunday-night 'check-in' has become a script that prevents the actual conversation
exampleSpecs.audience: a long-partnered couple whose ritual is doing the opposite of what it was built for
exampleSpecs.stakes: a marriage where the practice meant to keep them honest is now the alibi for not being
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one of them names the script out loud, and they agree to retire the format rather than perform it dead

exampleSpecs.domain: a fourth-year resident reviewing a missed diagnosis with her attending — a textbook presentation she pattern-matched in eight seconds and got wrong
exampleSpecs.audience: a high-performer whose speed is now the problem
exampleSpecs.stakes: a patient sent home with a condition the resident would have caught in her first year, when she was still slow
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she traces the error to the loss of a deliberate step she used to perform and reinstalls it as a non-negotiable, even at the cost of speed

exampleSpecs.domain: a long-distance runner in year seven of the same Tuesday tempo, Thursday intervals, Sunday long-run cycle, watching her race times plateau for the third season
exampleSpecs.audience: an amateur athlete who confused consistency with progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: another year of training that will produce another year of the same finish times
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she keeps the habit of showing up but rebuilds the contents of the week so the workload is uncomfortable again, and tracks the first month of returning soreness as evidence she is learning
